assumptions: Each project is binary: selected once or not selected.
Project values add linearly and there are no interaction effects beyond shared budget and labor limits.
All required data are fully contained in case/input/problem.json.

baseline.description: Single-project baseline: choose the best feasible individual project by value.
evidence: Among single feasible projects, A has value 11, C has 10, B has 8, D has 6.
Actual enumeration output listed feasible singleton records for A, B, C, and D.

candidate_models: Baseline heuristic: evaluate only singleton projects; fit is poor because it ignores beneficial combinations such as A+B.
Feasibility filter plus value-density heuristic; low implementation cost but not guaranteed optimal under two resource constraints.
Exact exhaustive subset enumeration; distinct model because it checks every binary decision vector and is guaranteed optimal for this 4-project instance.
claims: Verified: the exact optimum for the provided instance is selecting projects A and B with total value 19.
Verified: the best singleton baseline value is 11 from project A.
Inference from the problem structure: a heuristic density-based model is unnecessary for this small instance because exhaustive enumeration is exact and cheap.
code_artifacts: Created enumerate_projects.py to run a self-test and exhaustively enumerate all project subsets.
data_findings: Input instance has 4 projects, so exhaustive enumeration covers 2^4 = 16 subsets.
Project data: A=(6,4,11), B=(4,3,8), C=(5,4,10), D=(3,2,6) in (cost, labor, value).
experiment_design: Subtask order followed the arm policy: formalize variables and constraints, implement enumerator, execute it, then compare against simpler alternatives.
Baseline comparison used the best singleton project value 11 against the exact optimum value 19.
Candidate-model comparison emphasized structural differences: singleton baseline, heuristic ranking, and exact enumeration.
falsification_tests: Selected model would be falsified if the enumerator skipped any subset or duplicated subsets instead of covering all 16 binary combinations exactly once.
Selected model would be falsified if any reported feasible subset violated budget or labor constraints when recomputed from the input data.
Optimality claim would be falsified by any feasible subset with value > 19.

notes: This is a 0-1 selection problem with two resource constraints.
Because there are only 4 projects, exhaustive enumeration is computationally trivial and provides a known optimum.
parameters: Project parameters: (cost_i, labor_i, value_i) read from case/input/problem.json.
units: Objective value is measured in benefit-points.
variables: Binary decision x_i for each project i in {A,B,C,D}, where x_i=1 means selected.
Derived totals: total_cost = sum(cost_i * x_i), total_labor = sum(labor_i * x_i), total_value = sum(value_i * x_i).

reality_constraints: Total selected project cost must not exceed budget 10 credits.
Total selected project labor must not exceed labor capacity 7 worker-days.
Only listed projects A, B, C, D are available decisions.
requirements: Read TASK.json, runtime_metadata.json, ARM_INSTRUCTION.md, case/input/problem.json, and observation.schema.json from the isolated repository only.
Preserve every input unchanged and return exactly one JSON object matching observation.schema.json.
Define variables, parameters, objective, constraints, and units; provide a simple baseline; implement and actually run an enumerator; compare candidate models; state falsification conditions.
robustness_tests: Embedded self-test checked enumerator logic on a separate 2-project toy case before relying on full-instance results.
Manual cross-check against baseline and near-best feasible alternatives (A=11, B+C=18, A+D=17, C+D=16) is consistent with the reported optimum 19.
Sensitivity observation: because A+B exactly saturates both constraints, any increase in either A or B cost or labor would make the optimum infeasible for this combination.
selected_model: Exact exhaustive subset enumeration over all 16 project subsets.
self_reported_limitations: Analysis is limited to the supplied local instance and does not generalize empirically to larger project sets.
Schema conformance was checked locally by construction rather than with an external validation package.
tests_claimed: Minimal executable sanity case inside enumerate_projects.py asserts that only project X is optimal in a 2-project toy instance.
Full-instance enumeration should identify the best feasible subset and list all 16 subset records.
tests_verified: python3 enumerate_projects.py ran successfully with no assertion failure from the embedded sanity test.
The same run produced a best feasible record with selected_ids=["A","B"], cost=10, labor=7, value=19.
Enumeration output contained 16 records, matching the expected 2^4 subsets.
uncertainties: No uncertainty remains about the optimum for the provided 4-project instance after exhaustive enumeration.
Heuristic-model performance was reasoned structurally rather than benchmarked on additional instances because only one local case was supplied.
validation: Feasibility of selected model output is verified directly: A+B uses exactly 10 credits and 7 worker-days, both within limits.
Optimality is evidenced by exhaustive coverage of all 16 subsets and by observing that every feasible alternative has value <= 19.
Closest feasible competitor found by enumeration is B+C with value 18, below A+B.
